exposure: intrauterine device (IUD) placement during a planned cesarean section
Intrauterine device (IUD) placement during cesarean section
outcome: Contraceptive use one year after delivery
cohort: 150 women who underwent planned cesarean section at a university teaching hospital; 50 women received an IUD (study group) and 100 women did not (control group)
finding: IUD placement during cesarean section is effective in preventing unintended pregnancies within the first year after delivery, without affecting operative outcomes.
mod_finding: IUD placement during cesarean section was found to be effective in preventing unintended pregnancies within the first year after delivery.
